newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Cayman's electric company reports net earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Cayman's electric company reports net earnings up.

text.p: Caribbean Utilities Company (CUC) the sole supplier of power to this British Caribbean territory, announced net earnings for the first three quarters of this fiscal year were up 4.9 per cent from levels the previous year.

CUC said net earnings for the first three fiscal quarters of their accounting year that ended on Jan 31 1997 rose 4.9 percent to US$4.7 million compared with US$7.06 million against the same period in 1996.
The company also announced a dividend of US$.1625 per class A ordinary share.

CUC stock is traded on the Toronto stock exchange. It operates under a 25-year exclusive contract with the Cayman Islands government that guarantees the company a 15 per cent rate of return on investment. The company can arbitrarily raise its electrical rates each year to meet the guaranteed rate of return.
For 1996, the company generated just over US$60 million in sales. Sales in 1997 are expected to be near the US$65 million mark.

The Class A stock of CUC is currently trading at US$15 per share up from US$ a share in October 1994 when the class A stock underwent a two-for-one split. Analysts expect another split in the near future if the stock climbs over US$17 per share as expected.
